title: Guinea-Bissau’s military government pushes elections back to 2028
seoTitle: Guinea-Bissau election delay: why the vote moved to 2028
dek: A decree moves the presidential and legislative elections from December 2026 to November 2028, extending the military-led transition by almost two years.
happened: Guinea-Bissau’s transitional president issued a decree on November 26 moving both national elections to November 26, 2028. The vote had been scheduled for December 6, 2026. The announcement came a year after the military removed President Umaro Sissoco Embaló and halted the release of the previous election’s results.

sides.says: The decree said the country lacked the funding and practical preparations needed to run a credible election. The transitional president said changes to voter registration and electoral boundaries would take more time and resources.
The Economic Community of West African States had previously urged a brief and transparent transition back to civilian government.

AFP reported that opposition parties called for a boycott of the August constitutional referendum. The PAIGC party said the referendum took place while restrictions on public freedoms were still in effect.

next: The decree sets a new national election date of November 26, 2028. AFP reported that the military government also plans municipal elections in 2027 and a nationwide update of the voter register.
summary: Guinea-Bissau’s military government delayed the elections intended to restore civilian rule. The new date is November 2028.
